investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and all sibling remote-agent checks) failed at 2026-06-15T08:59:09.842Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a successful agent creation response, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected and all contract assertions went unverified. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real API-level quota constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with a 409 Conflict because the org used by the observability probe has reached or exceeded the swarm agent quota limit of 100. Because agent creation failed at the API boundary, the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 808: createAgent call) never obtained an agent record, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated and causing the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks to fail with the identical 409 message. The root cause is a quota exhaustion condition on the probe org's agent count in the production-api environment, not a code defect in the eval runner itself.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the API rejected the creation request before any agent was provisioned.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: All four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting immediately on the 409 before any evidence could be written.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: Both sibling checks carry the identical 409 message (sameMessage=true, evidenceKeys=[]), confirming the failure originates at the shared createAgent call upstream of all three checks, not in check-specific logic.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:800-808: The runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 808; a 409 at that call would propagate as the check failure message before any evidence is recorded.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1191 — the call returned in ~1.2 s, consistent with a fast synchronous quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or VM provisioning failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:102-110: The contract at lines 106-111 requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the agent was never created.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Probe org agent quota exhausted: The org used by the observability probe has accumulated 100 or more swarm agents (possibly from prior eval runs whose cleanup step failed or was skipped), causing every new POST /api/agents to be rejected with 409. This is directly stated in the error body and explains the identical failure across all three sibling checks.

SECONDARY — Eval cleanup not running or incomplete: The withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 806) is responsible for deleting agents after each probe run. If cleanup failed silently in previous runs, leaked agents would accumulate against the quota until the limit is reached.

TERTIARY — Probe org misconfigured with a low or shared quota: The probe org may share its agent quota with other workloads or may have been provisioned with a quota that is too low for repeated observability runs, making quota exhaustion more likely.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Regression introduced by commit 6b9c8b0 (feat(observability): separate feature health from runtime evidence, #63): This commit touched all three implicated eval files ~18 minutes before the failure. However, the commit's listed touchedPaths contain only CI workflow and config files, with no candidateTouchedPaths or matchedNeedles in the eval runner or cleanup logic. The 409 error is a clear API-level quota signal, not a runner logic error, so this commit is not supported as causal by the current evidence.

investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with a 409 Conflict because the org used by the observability probe has reached or exceeded the swarm agent quota limit of 100. The root cause is a quota exhaustion condition on the probe org's agent count in the production-api environment, not a code defect in the eval runner itself.

Because the session could not be opened, no generation frames were produced, and the contract assertions for frameTypes (must contain generation_completed) and imageUrlPresent (must equal true) could not be satisfied. This is an eval infrastructure / harness reachability failure localized to the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence to indicate a user-facing outage.
